title: This Parasite Eats a Fish's Tongue, Then Becomes Its New Tongue
subject: snapper fish

scenes.text: There is a parasite that swaps a fish's tongue for itself.
It starts as a tiny larva that swims in through the fish's gills.
It crawls into the mouth and clamps onto the tongue with its claws.
That cuts off the blood, and the tongue withers and drops away.
The parasite grips the stub and takes over the job. Scientists call it the only known parasite to replace a host organ.
Then it lives there for years, feeding on blood and mucus. The fish's new tongue is alive.

description:
The tongue-eating louse enters a fish through the gills, cuts off its tongue's blood supply, then takes the tongue's place.
Scientists call it the only known case of a parasite functionally replacing a host organ.
Would you want to know what your fish is hiding?
first_comment: Which animal would you least want as a lodger: this parasite or the lamprey?
